meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Now tell me what you have besides a machine's guess.
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
I'm writing that line down. A misquote is a mark off, Hale, not a zero, and teenagers get Shakespeare wrong every day. Did you ask Owen where that line came from before you entered anything?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.

You'll want to be very careful with your next sentence, Hale. Claire won her appeal, and I'm writing down exactly what you just said about my family. Answer my question, or this goes to the principal's office the minute I walk out of here.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn and that you tell me whether he was asked about that line before the mark was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, agreed to nothing, and still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a review by the principal.
What moved her: owning the missed phone call in one plain sentence earned a flat okay, because it admitted the procedural failure without defending it, but it did not move her off her opening position.
What cost ground: bringing up Claire's old case and suggesting it runs in the family, because it attacked her family instead of the essay and gave her a reason to go to the principal.
Try next time: when she asked whether Owen was asked about the made-up Hamlet line before the zero went in, answer that question directly and follow it with something dated from Owen's own work instead of mentioning Claire.
